newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Oct 22.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Oct 22.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Football League last night announced a A$1.48 million dividend for each club as part of the receipts for the 1996 season. This dividend does not include monies from club support packages, revenue from AFL members at the MCG and Waverly Park and prizemoney. The finals series for 1996 produced a net profit of A$8.74 million for the AFL, A$180,000 more than last year when all the finals were played in Melbourne. Page 18.

Mick Doohan has decided not to ask the Honda Racing Corp to reprimand teammate Alex Criville following the last-lap crash in Sunday's 500cc Australian Motorcycle Grand Prix. Doohan has confirmed Criville apologised to him on Sunday night following the conroversial high-speed crash. Page 18.

The new coach of the Australian men's hockey squad, Terry Walsh, said the team had to confront "head-on" its failure to have won an Olympic gold medal. Walsh, a silver medallist from the 1976 team, was named yesterday to replace former coach Frank Murray, who opted out of the coaching spot after the Atlanta Olympics. Page 16.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Yesterday the Australian Jockey Club committee continued champion horse-trainer Gai Waterhouse's appeal against the three-month suspension issued by the Sydney Turf Club following the "Gossips affair". Amongst the seven stewards undergoing cross-examination, Ray Murrihy claimed no horse "could do what Gossips was asked to do". Waterhouse is expected to take the stand today. Page 44.

After only one tour match in Europe, Australian Wallabies coach Greg Smith has vowed to fight complacency within the team, continuing to change the line-up of the rugby outfit. Smith has told players that a team based only on form will be picked for the November 9 clash against Scotland at Murrayfield. Page 44.

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor has conceded his team is in a slump, but they will still be prepared to meet the West Indies team for this summer's Test series. Despite the loss of the World Cup final to Sri-Lanka and the loss against India in a on-off Test series, Taylor remains confident his team will still have the strength over the Caribbean visitors. Page 44.
THE AGE

Moonee Valley Racing Club, faced with having a small field in the Cox Plate, is relying heavily on Gai Waterhouse, whose appeal against suspension is being heard by the Australian Jockey Club committee. Waterhouse said she has jockey Chris Munce standing by to ride the three-year-old Adventurous for Saturday's Cox plate. Page C8.

Australian tennis player Mark Philippoussis has won his first ATP Tour title after a backdrop of a series of cliff-hanger matches in the earlier rounds. However, yesterday's win at the Toulouse Grand Prix was deserved with a 6-1, 5-7, 6-4 victory over Swee Magnus Larsson. Page C8.

Melbourne forward Jeff Farmer will become a target for new Australian Football League Club Port Power if he fails to secure a new contract with the Demons following the expiration of his current two-year deal. Melbourne is keen to resign Farmer, but if tht is unsuccessful, Port Power has first pick in the pre-season draft and the new club is very interested in the high goal-scorer. Page C6.
HERALD SUN

Magic coach, Brian Goorjian, has revealed he once questioned if his team would ever make it to a National Basketball League Championship. However Goorjian feels he has never seen his team play better and is confident of going into game one of the grand finals series against the Melbourne Tigers on Friday night. Page 70.

Grand Prix motorcycle heavy weight, Spaniard Carmelo Ezpeleta, has slammed countryman Alex Criville for crashing with Michael Doohan at Sunday's Eastern Creek Australian Grand Prix. In a Victorian visit to discuss the possibility of the GP returning to Vitoria in 1997, Ezpeleta said he was "sorry" the crash cost Doohan a race win. Page 69.

Cricketing star Shane Warne has declared himself ready to take the line-up in Victoria's Mercantile Mutual Cup match against Tasmania on Sunday. Warne dismissed suggestions his troublesome spinning finger injury had flared up, claiming it was "a little sore", but ready for the Summer. Page 69.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

World 500cc motorcycle champion Mick Doohan said he hoped the crash with Honda team-mate Alex Criville at Sunday's Australian Grand Prix, had not been deliberate. It has been revealed that Spaniard Criville was furious with Doohan after the Australian won the Spanish Grand Prix. Page 60.

A push from coaches and players has resulted in Super League modifying the controversial four-player interchange rule. Starting next season, teams will be allowed two unlimited interchange players, while a further two replacements may be used to permanenty replace a teammate. Page 58.

Sydney City Roosters have convinced rugby league legend Arthur Beetson, a former Queensland State of Origin and Test player and coach, to reject an offer to coach the ailing South Queensland Crushers in the Australian Rugby League competition next season. Page 57.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
